SMTO-HTTP-0038 — SMTO couldn't find the service's sign-in address

GUID: 940b94f1-edd1-45c3-83b1-81d641e46322
Slug: http-auth-endpoint-not-found
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The address SMTO uses to sign in doesn't exist on the service. This usually means the sign-in address is wrong, not that your password is.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and check Base URL and the sign-in address: Login path for a login form, or Token endpoint for OAuth. The service reported that nothing exists at the address SMTO used to sign in.
  2. Compare those addresses with the service's official documentation, or ask its owner for the correct sign-in address. Services sometimes move their sign-in address between versions.
  3. Save, then select Test connection. When it shows Authenticated, run the task again. This confirms the corrected address works before the task uses it.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Authenticated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't keep changing the password or sending the same sign-in; the address is the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The authentication endpoint (login path or OAuth token endpoint) returned HTTP 404 instead of a configured success status.

What this means

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 404 instead of a configured success status. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The authentication endpoint returned HTTP 404 instead of a configured success status.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the resolved login URL, base-path rules and reverse-proxy route; this response does not prove invalid credentials.

How to fix it

  • Correct the profile's login path, token_endpoint or issuer discovery URL against the target's API documentation, and confirm base_url includes any required path prefix. A 404 does not indicate invalid credentials.
  • Correct the authentication endpoint using the service’s authoritative API documentation. A missing endpoint does not prove credentials are wrong.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The documented authentication endpoint is reached through the intended route.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
